claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in refractory high-entropy alloys are governed by a stable distribution of coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the alloy.
Coherent nanoprecipitates provide pathways for dislocation transfer that enhance ductility and toughness.
Powder mixing and spark plasma sintering can produce a uniform refractory HEA microstructure containing a fine, initially coherent nanoprecipitate distribution.
A targeted aging treatment can preserve and refine precipitate coherence and uniformity.
An alternative aging treatment can promote precipitate coarsening and loss of coherence.
Mechanical testing at 600–800°C under controlled strain rate and inert atmosphere replicates thermal-mechanical conditions expected in fusion plasma-facing components.
Refractory HEAs can retain high hardness and high compressive yield strength in the 600–800°C range.
Refractory high-temperature alloys of this class are candidates for fusion-reactor structural applications.
Coherent nanoprecipitates increase yield strength by acting as barriers to dislocation motion.
Coherent nanoprecipitates increase strain hardening.
Coherent precipitate interfaces allow dislocations to bypass obstacles without producing local stress concentrations.
The combination of impeded dislocation motion and stress-relieving dislocation transfer delays plastic instability and crack initiation.
Maintaining a fine coherent nanoprecipitate network will produce higher yield strength than a coarsened, incoherent precipitate structure.
Maintaining a fine coherent nanoprecipitate network will produce greater strain hardening than a coarsened, incoherent precipitate structure.
Maintaining a fine coherent nanoprecipitate network will produce greater plastic strain, energy absorption, and toughness than a coarsened, incoherent precipitate structure.
Standard processing without specialized aging produces a less optimized, partially coarsened precipitate structure.
The coherent precipitate structure remains sufficiently stable for the proposed mechanism to operate up to approximately 800°C.
Grain-boundary sliding or twinning may also contribute to high-temperature plastic strain and toughness.
Prior evidence supports the proposed dual strengthening and toughening role of coherent nanoprecipitates.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as material processed without specialized aging, but the experimental comparison designated as the control is actively aged to induce coarsening and incoherence. Thus, the proposed two-group experiment does not actually include the stated unperturbed baseline.
